description: Run one real check of a target from one region chosen by Fettle, without creating anything. It reports status (up, down, error or unknown), region, response_time_ms, status_code, error and failure_kind. unknown means no definite answer came back, not a failure. Use it before create_monitor to catch a typo or an unreachable host; a down result does not stop you creating the monitor. For a monitor that already exists use check_now. Requires a key with the write scope. It is rate limited per calling address: a 429 whose retry_after says how many seconds to wait. Example: {"type": "HTTP", "target": "https://api.example.com/health"}

config.description: As in create_monitor; TCP and DNS need it. The region, interval and update rules there do not apply to a one-off probe. An object whose fields depend on type, all optional unless stated. HTTP: method (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, any case; default GET); expected_status_codes (non-empty list of codes 100 to 599, default [200]); keyword (case-sensitive substring the body must contain, at most 1024 characters, not with HEAD); follow_redirects (default true); verify_ssl (default true; false skips TLS verification, so the monitor can never report TLS_INVALID); request_headers (object of name to value: at most 20, a name at most 128 characters of letters, digits and ! # $ % & ' * + - . ^ _ ` | ~, a value at most 1024 bytes of printable ASCII, space or tab, the whole object at most 8192 bytes as JSON; names differing only in case, and Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Upgrade, TE, Trailer, Keep-Alive, CF-Connecting-IP or any Proxy-* name, are a 422); request_body (string, at most 8192 bytes as UTF-8, needs POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE). Reads return every request_headers value as the literal __FETTLE_UNCHANGED__; writing that literal back in an update keeps the stored value (on create it is a 422). PING: packet_count (1 to 20, default 4). SSL: warn_before_days (1 to 365, default 14) and port (1 to 65535, default 443). TCP: either port (1 to 65535) with expected_state "open" (default) or "closed", or ports (1 to 20 distinct ports that must all be closed, which needs expected_state "closed", exactly one region and interval_seconds of at least 300; a check fails when any of them accepts a connection, and the monitor goes DOWN once confirmation_threshold failures confirm it). Both port and ports, or neither, is a 422; expected_state values are lowercase. DNS: record_type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT or NS; required) and expected_value (at most 2048 characters). With expected_value one answer must equal it (case-insensitive, ignoring surrounding spaces and a trailing dot; exact for TXT); without it any answer passes. MX answers are the mail host names without priority (mail.example.com, not 10 mail.example.com). A and AAAA look up every address of the host, IPv4 and IPv6 alike, and any one may match; write an IPv6 address in its shortest form.

target.description: What to check, up to 2048 characters. HTTP: an http:// or https:// URL (https:// is added when the scheme is missing; port, path and query are kept). PING, SSL, TCP and DNS: a bare public hostname or IP address with no :port and no path (the port goes in config): host:port is a 422, and a full URL is cut down to its host, losing its port. Hostnames are ASCII (punycode for internationalized domains). localhost, *.localhost and addresses that are not public (private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, reserved, unspecified) are a 422.

type.description: HTTP (a URL answers with an expected status), PING (a host answers ICMP), SSL (a certificate is valid and not about to expire), TCP (a port is open, or a list of ports is closed) or DNS (a record resolves, optionally to an expected value).

name: check_target

anyOf.description: Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, UNKNOWN.

status.description: Known values: up, down, error, unknown.

title: Probe a target before creating a monitor
